records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without validating the URL scheme, unlike TopicEmbed.import; since Kernel#open treats leading '|' as a shell command, this allows command injection via crafted URLs (including from lib/tasks/disqus.thor)
records.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` directly does `open(url).read` with no `http/https` scheme validation, unlike `TopicEmbed.import` which checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Since Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats strings starting with `|` as a shell pipe, a crafted `url` could trigger command execution. records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import performs a non-atomic check-then-create on embed_url, so concurrent callers can both pass the blank? check and both call create!, causing an unhandled RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid due to the unique index on embed_url
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if `embed.blank?`, creates a new record with `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. records.issue_text: embed.js uses document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without checking for null, so a missing element causes comments.appendChild(iframe) to throw and can break the rest of the host page's script execution
records.rationale: In new app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is used immediately with `comments.appendChild(iframe);` and there is no null/undefined guard. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, this will throw a TypeError and can break subsequent script execution on that page.

records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header to restrict access, which is attacker-controlled and doesn't reliably prevent arbitrary URLs from triggering Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)
records.rationale: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable gates access by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but `Referer` is a client-supplied header and can be spoofed. With a forged Referer matching the configured host, an attacker can reach `EmbedController#best` and trigger `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` when no embed exists.
